title: Microsoft 365 admin center: pay for Copilot Chat from prepaid capacity packs alone
summary: Held because Microsoft documents Global Administrator as required for creating a credit policy, but does not establish the same exclusive requirement for editing or deleting one. The cost classification also conflicts with the wiki's metered-cost definition; the standalone billing behaviour and the allocation API are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans prepaid capacity as the sole billing method for supported Copilot experiences, with no pay-as-you-go charges for users in the policy.
claims.quote: Admins can configure billing policies with prepaid capacity such that usage for users in the policy is deducted exclusively from prepaid capacity credits, with no pay as you go charges.

claims.fix: Remove 'edit' from the Scope role requirement. Keep 'Global Administrator to create a policy and to enable capacity pack usage'; the cited capacity-packs page establishes those tasks, not an exclusive editing role.

claims.claim: Deleting a Copilot credit policy requires Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot credit policy" "delete" "role"; opened capacity-packs and usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup. No passage establishes an exclusive Global Administrator requirement for deleting a Copilot credit policy.
claims.fix: Remove 'delete' from the Scope role requirement. Keep 'Global Administrator to create a policy and to enable capacity pack usage'; do not transfer the creation requirement to deletion.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center path reaches creation of a credit policy that scopes prepaid usage to users.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Billing & usage. Select the Pay-as-you-go services tab, and then select Microsoft Copilot Chat. In the Copilot credit policies section, select Create a Copilot credit policy.
claims.fix: Extend the existing path with '> Scope' to reach the scoping control documented on the cited page. Add a note that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot gives the alternate entry 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage', whereas the capacity-packs page gives 'Copilot > Billing & usage', and cite that page.

claims.claim: No API for creating or editing these Copilot credit policies is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot credit policies create edit API Microsoft Graph prepaid capacity user groups; opened capacity-packs, Cost Management API overview and the Power Platform allocations tutorial. Found spending-policy APIs, not an API identified as these credit policies.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center route reaches the billing policy Connection status toggle for Copilot Chat overage billing.
claims.quote: On the Pay-as-you-go services tab for Microsoft Copilot Chat, find the billing policy name to bill for any overage, then switch the Connection status toggle to Connected.
claims.fix: Keep the supported path but note the alternative 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage' entry in https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot, which differs from the capacity-packs page's 'Copilot > Billing & usage' entry. Cite that page; the same navigation note can cover both Microsoft 365 control rows.

claims.claim: No API is documented for the classic Copilot Chat billing-policy connection toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot Chat pay as you go billing policy Connection status API connect disconnect Graph; Copilot billing policy connect API Power Platform. Opened Cost Management API overview and pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot; no API for the classic connection toggle.

claims.claim: The printed Power Platform admin center route reaches Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: On the Summary tab, under Capacity summary, find the Prepaid Capacity card. In the License type column, select Manage capacity. Under Capacity overages, select the options for what happens when capacity reaches zero.
claims.fix: Keep the path supported by the capacity-packs page. Add: 'The programmatic-allocation tutorial gives another UI route: Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.' The tutorial is already cited at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations.

claims.claim: PUT /licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the MCSMessages allocation and its TenantPool enforcement rule.
claims.quote:
All programmatic examples in this article use API version `2024-10-01`.
...
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
claims.fix: Keep the call: the pre-check's literal-string miss is not a missing operation. Replace the first sentence of the note with 'For entitlementId MCSMessages, the request body sets allocatedEntitlements[].enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled true or false.' The tutorial documents these properties in its PowerShell request body.

claims.claim: The Capacity overages pane offers both tenant-capacity draw and Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan, and allows either or both.
claims.quote: Under Capacity overages, select the options for what happens when capacity reaches zero. You can choose one or both of the following options: Draw from the available capacity in my tenant. Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explain the precedence between a standalone user credit policy and the environment's separate pay-as-you-go overage selection.
claims.quote: Searched: standalone Copilot credit policy Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan TenantPool capacity overages interaction. Opened capacity-packs and allocations tutorial; read billing-rates and harness cost-control results. No passage resolves standalone-policy precedence.

claims.claim: Draw from the available capacity in my tenant maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule.
claims.quote: The Draw from the available capacity in my tenant option in the admin center maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule

claims.claim: Enabling TenantPool permits consumption from unallocated tenant capacity after the environment allocation runs out.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.claim: Disabling TenantPool caps the environment at its allocation, as the tutorial states.
claims.quote: when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.
claims.fix: Replace the cap clause with 'when it is disabled, prepaid consumption is capped at the allocation; usage can still continue through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness, whose Manage allocations across many environments section states that qualification, alongside the tutorial's broader wording.

claims.claim: A published environment group rule can lock the tenant-capacity setting and individual updates fail with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: The cited allocation tutorial documents the tenant-capacity option, not automation for the separate pay-as-you-go overage option.
claims.quote: Searched: "programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations" "pay-as-you-go"; read the entire tutorial, including all SDK examples. Its enforcement examples set TenantPool; none sets the separate pay-as-you-go option.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends using roles with the fewest permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft recommends that you use roles with the fewest permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises limiting Global Administrator to emergency scenarios when an existing role cannot be used.
claims.quote: Global Administrator is a highly privileged role that should be limited to emergency scenarios when you can't use an existing role.

claims.claim: Copilot Cost Management spending policies can use prepaid capacity packs as their billing method.
claims.quote: You can choose to apply Prepaid Capacity packs at the individual spending policy level in the Review billing method step.

claims.claim: The spending-policy setup page recommends enabling a pay-as-you-go meter for continuity after capacity pack credits are exhausted.
claims.quote: Enable a pay-as-you-go meter to ensure your services continue once Prepaid Capacity pack credits are exhausted.

claims.claim: The Learn capacity-packs page does not describe credit policies as granting access to data.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot credit policy Global Administrator edit delete data access permissions grants. Read capacity-packs in full and the returned permission excerpts; it describes credit funding, user scope and service availability, not new data permissions.

claims.claim: The groups' membership determines which users the credit policy covers and whose consumption uses its credits.
claims.quote: Each Copilot credit policy is scoped to specific user groups. When a user interacts with Copilot Chat, the system uses credits from the policy that covers that user.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Learn's what's-new page lists standalone capacity pack usage under April 2026 and describes it as supported.
claims.quote: April 2026. Copilot capacity pack without pay-as-you-go. Microsoft 365 Copilot now supports standalone capacity pack usage, enabling organizations to consume prepaid Copilot Credits without requiring pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The medium cost rating fits the documented Copilot Credits consumption model.
claims.quote: Front matter: cost: "medium"; licensing.model: "consumption". Body: "Copilot Credits are the unit of consumption." The standard defines variable as "metered (Copilot Credits, pay-as-you-go, Azure). Always name the meter."
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. Copilot Credits meter usage against prepaid capacity packs of 25,000 credits per month per pack; a standalone policy draws only on that prepaid pool.' Keep licensing.model as consumption.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the checklist tells readers to configure or monitor has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Allocate capacity"; "Monitor credits consumed and remaining"; "Set the Overage notification". Rows govern user credit policies, pay-as-you-go connections and tenant-capacity draw, not allocation quantities, usage monitoring or notifications.
claims.fix: The checklist steps 'Allocate capacity to the Copilot Chat environment', 'Monitor credits consumed and remaining' and 'Set the Overage notification' have no corresponding control rows. Row 3 covers tenant-capacity overages, not allocation quantities, usage monitoring or notifications.

claims.claim: The Overage notification setting can notify administrators when capacity usage nears a selected percentage.
claims.quote: Under Overage notification, select the Send notification when nearing capacity usage checkbox, and then select a percentage value from the drop-down list.

claims.claim: Billing and AI administrators can set up pay-as-you-go billing but cannot activate a capacity pack.
claims.quote: Billing administrators or AI administrators can set up pay-as-you-go billing but can't activate a capacity pack.
